'''''Melaleuca linearis''''', commonly known as '''narrow-leaved bottlebrush''', is a plant in the myrtle [[Family (taxonomy)|family]], [[Myrtaceae]] and is [[Endemism|endemic]] to [[New South Wales]] and [[Queensland]] in Australia. It is a medium-sized shrub with narrow leaves with a rigid point, and red flower spikes in late spring or early summer.

==Description==
''Melaleuca linearis'' is a shrub growing to {{convert|3|m|ft|sigfig=1}} tall with grey, hard, fibrous bark. Its leaves are arranged alternately and are {{convert|35-115|mm|in|sigfig=1}} long, {{convert|0.7-2.7|mm|in|sigfig=1}} wide, narrow linear in shape and flat to channelled or semi-circular in cross section. There is a mid-vein but the lateral veins are inconspicuous.<ref name=Brophy>{{cite book|last1=Brophy|first1=Joseph J.|last2=Craven|first2=Lyndley A.|last3=Doran|first3=John C.|title=Melaleucas : their botany, essential oils and uses|date=2013|publisher=Australian Centre for International Agricultural Research|location=Canberra|isbn=9781922137517|pages=230–231}}</ref><ref name=RBGS>{{cite web|last1=Spencer|first1=Roger|last2=Lumley|first2=Peter F.|title=''Callistemon linearis'' (Schrad. & J.C.Wendl.) Colvill ex Sweet |url=http://plantnet.rbgsyd.nsw.gov.au/cgi-bin/NSWfl.pl?page=nswfl&lvl=sp&name=Callistemon~linearis|publisher=Royal Botanic Garden Sydney: Plantnet|access-date=14 July 2015}}</ref><ref name=ANPSA>{{cite web|title=''Callistemon linearis''|url=http://anpsa.org.au/c-lin.html|publisher=Australian Native Plants Society Australia|access-date=14 July 2015}}</ref>

The flowers are a shade of red, rarely green and arranged in spikes on the ends of branches that continue to grow after flowering and also on the sides of the branches. The spikes are {{convert|40-65|mm|in|sigfig=1}} in diameter and {{convert|5-10|cm|in|sigfig=2}} long with 20 to 90 individual flowers. The petals are {{convert|3.2-7|mm|in|sigfig=1}} long and fall off as the flower ages and there are 23–73 stamens in each flower. Flowering occurs from late spring to early summer and is followed by fruits that are woody [[Capsule (botany)|capsule]]s, {{convert|3.8-8.2|mm|in|sigfig=1}} long.<ref name="Brophy" /><ref name="RBGS" /><ref name="ANPSA" />

==Taxonomy and naming==
''Melaleuca linearis'' was first formally described in 1796 by [[Heinrich Schrader (botanist)|Heinrich Schrader]] and [[Johann Christoph Wendland]] in ''[[Sertum Hannoveranum]]''.<ref name=APNI(1)>{{cite web|title=''Melaleuca linearis''|url=  https://biodiversity.org.au/boa/instance/apni/514319|publisher=APNI|access-date=14 July 2015}}</ref><ref name=Sertum>{{cite book|last1=Schrader|first1=Heinrich|last2=Wendland|first2=Johann Christoph|title=Sertum Hannoveranum 2|date=1796|page=19|url=http://bibdigital.rjb.csic.es/ing/Libro.php?Libro=3957&Pagina=7|access-date=14 July 2015}}</ref> The [[Botanical name|specific epithet]] (''linearis'') is a [[Latin]] word ''linearis'' meaning "linear"<ref name="RWB">{{cite book|last1=Brown|first1=Roland Wilbur|title=The Composition of Scientific Words|date=1956|publisher=Smithsonian Institution Press|location=Washington, D.C.|page=485}}</ref> in reference to the shape of the leaves of this species.<ref name="Brophy" />

In 2006, Craven described two varieties of ''Melaleuca linearis'' in the journal ''[[Missouri_Botanical_Garden#Publications|Novon]]'':
* ''Melaleuca linearis'' <small>Schrad. & J.C.Wendl.</small> var. ''linearis''<ref name=APNI(2)>{{cite web|title=''Melaleuca linearis'' var. ''linearis''|url=  https://biodiversity.org.au/boa/instance/apni/662426|publisher=APNI|access-date=22 November 2021}}</ref> has leaves that are more than {{convert|1.3|mm|in|sigfig=1}} wide, usually 23–33 stamens per flower and occurs in Queensland south to the [[Coonabarabran]] and [[Narrabri]] districts in New South Wales and also in and between the [[Central Coast (New South Wales)|Central Coast]] and [[Nowra, New South Wales|Nowra]] districts in New South Wales.<ref name="Brophy" /> 
* ''Melaleuca linearis'' var. ''pinifolia'' <small>(J.C.Wendl.) Craven</small><ref name=APNI(3)>{{cite web|title=''Melaleuca linearis'' var. ''pinifolia''|url=  https://biodiversity.org.au/boa/instance/apni/613693|publisher=APNI|access-date=20 July 2015}}</ref> has leaves that are less than {{convert|1.3|mm|in|sigfig=1}} wide, 34–73 stamens per flower and occurs in the [[Gilgandra, New South Wales|Gilgandra]], [[Kandos, New South Wales|Kandos]] and [[Sydney]] districts in New South Wales.<ref name="Brophy" />

===Synonymy===
[[Plants of the World Online]] regards ''Callistemon linearis'' as a synonym of ''M. linearis'',<ref name="POWO1">{{cite web |title=''Callistemon linearis'' |url=https://powo.science.kew.org/results?q=Callistemon%20linearis |publisher=Plants of the World Online |access-date=22 November 2021}}</ref> ''C. pinifolius'' as a synonym of ''M. linearis'' var. ''acerosa'' (although this variety, named by [[Ignaz Friedrich Tausch|Tausch]] has not been formally described)<ref name="POWO2">{{cite web |title=''Callistemon pinifolius'' |url=https://powo.science.kew.org/results?q=Callistemon%20pinifolius |publisher=Plants of the World Online |access-date=22 November 2021}}</ref> and ''C. rigidus'' as a synonym of ''M. linearis'' var. ''linearis''.<ref name="POWO3">{{cite web |title=''Callistemon rigidus'' |url=https://powo.science.kew.org/results?q=Callistemon%20rigidus |publisher=Plants of the World Online |access-date=22 November 2021}}</ref> It further considers ''M. linearis'' var. ''pinifolia'' to be a synonym of ''M. linearis'' var. ''acerosa''.<ref name="POWO11">{{cite web |title=''Melaleuca linearis'' var. ''pinifolia'' |url=https://powo.science.kew.org/results?q=Melaleuca%20linearis%20var.%20pinifolia |publisher=Plants of the World Online |access-date=22 November 2021}}</ref> However, the [[National Herbarium of New South Wales]] retains the names ''Callistemon linearis'',<ref name=RBGS(1)>{{cite web|title=''Callistemon linearis''|url=http://plantnet.rbgsyd.nsw.gov.au/cgi-bin/NSWfl.pl?page=nswfl&lvl=sp&name=Callistemon~linearis|publisher=Royal Botanic Gardens Sydney:Plantnet|access-date=21 July 2015}}</ref> ''Callistemon pinifolius''<ref name=RBGS(2)>{{cite web |title=''Callistemon pinifolius'' (J.C.Wendl.) ==Distribution and habitat==
''Melaleuca linearis'' occurs in and between the south-east corner of Queensland, [[Nowra, New South Wales|Nowra]] on the south coast of New South Wales and inland as far as [[Gilgandra, New South Wales|Gilgandra]]. It grows in damp situations in a range of vegetation associations.<ref name="Brophy" /><ref name="RBGS" />

==Use in horticulture==
''Melaleuca linearis'' has long been in cultivation (as ''Callistemon linearis'', ''C. pinifolius'' and ''C. rigidus''). Although not common in gardens, it is a hardy plant, thriving in most soils but preferring full sun. It is more resistant to pests such as [[sawfly]] than other melaleucas.<ref name="ANPSA" /><ref name=Wrigley>{{cite book|last1=Wrigley|first1=John W.|last2=Fagg|first2=Murray|title=Australian native plants : a manual for their propagation, cultivation and use in landscaping|date=1983|publisher=Collins|location=Sydney|isbn=0002165759|pages=192–193|edition=2nd}}</ref> It has received the [[Royal Horticultural Society]]'s [[Award of Garden Merit]].<ref name = RHSPF>{{cite web | url = https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/2689/Callistemon-linearis/Details | title = ''Callistemon linearis'' | website = www.rhs.org | publisher = Royal Horticultural Society | access-date = 12 April 2020}}</ref>
